title: Customer Insights - Journeys: Journey Creation Agent builds journeys from a plain-language description
notes: claim 77: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the credit-allocation API example omits the request body needed to run it, and the agent-enablement path omits the Overview tab. The page also incorrectly treats EU Data Boundary tenants as unable to use Anthropic and promises a spending cap while elsewhere saying that cap is unconfirmed.

claims.claim: Journey Creation Agent is an AI assistant that drafts customer journeys from plain-language conversation.
claims.quote: Journey Creation Agent is an AI-powered assistant in Dynamics 365 Customer Insights - Journeys that lets you build customer journey structures through natural language conversation.

claims.claim: The agent proposes journey steps, timing and branching logic.
claims.quote: Describe your journey in conversational language and the agent proposes a journey structure with steps, timing, and branching logic.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn documents the feature as preview, with prerelease behaviour subject to change.
claims.quote: [This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.claim: Journey Creation Agent replaces the previously released Journey Copilot for journey creation.
claims.quote: Journey Creation Agent replaces the previously released Journey Copilot for journey creation.

claims.claim: The agent assembles journeys using segments and content assets that already exist in the environment.
claims.quote: The agent works with segments and content assets that already exist in your Customer Insights - Journeys environment.

claims.quote: it doesn't create segments or write content for you in this release.

claims.quote: Before you publish, the agent presents a visual preview of the proposed journey.

claims.claim: Selecting Review and refine opens the proposal on the standard journey designer.
claims.quote: select **Review and refine** in the agent panel. The journey opens on the standard journey canvas with all proposed steps, conditions, and content assignments populated.

claims.claim: Nothing goes live until a person approves the journey and publishes it as usual.
claims.quote: Nothing goes live until you approve it. ... When the journey structure is correct, you can publish the journey as you usually would.

claims.quote: Journey Creation Agent is currently available only in English.

claims.claim: Learn says North America and Oceania customers get Journey Creation Agent with the June 2026 update.
claims.quote: If you're a customer in the North America (NAM) or Oceania (OCE) region, Journey Creation Agent will be available to you with the June 2026 update.

claims.claim: The feature requires update 1.1.65002.153, installed through Settings > Versions.
claims.quote: To use Journey Creation Agent, navigate to **Settings** > **Versions** and upgrade to 1.1.65002.153.

claims.quote: Prompts that contain personally identifiable information (PII) or sensitive data may be blocked.

claims.claim: The agent may omit steps using an unconfigured channel.
claims.quote: If you referenced a channel not yet configured (for example, push notifications when no push app is set up), the agent may omit those steps.

claims.quote: Preview features aren’t meant for production use and might have restricted functionality.

claims.claim: Refreshing the creation experience discards a proposal unless it was transferred to the journey builder through Review and refine.
claims.quote: Refreshing the page while on the creation experience discards the current proposal. If the proposal was already transferred to the journey builder by selecting **Review and refine**, your work is preserved.

claims.claim: If a mandatory prerequisite is no longer accepted, enabled agents are automatically disabled until it is accepted again.
claims.quote: If any mandatory prerequisite is no longer accepted ... All enabled agents are *automatically disabled*. ... Agents remain unavailable until the prerequisite is accepted again.

claims.quote: If a tenant administrator disables AI agents in the **Power Platform Admin Center**: ... All active agents are **immediately disabled**.

claims.claim: Tenant-level disabling prevents new agents from being created or configured.
claims.quote: New agents can't be created or configured.

claims.claim: An individual agent can be disabled in AI Hub > Add and manage agents > agent by setting its status to Disabled.
claims.quote: In AI Hub, go to **Add and manage agents**. ... Select the agent. ... Set the agent status to **Disabled**.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: A feature-specific per-journey credit quantity or price is not published in the documentation checked.
claims.quote: Searched: Journey Creation Agent Copilot credits per journey price rate billing. Opened journey-creation-agent, ai-hub-prerequisites and microsoft-copilot-studio/billing-licensing; billing-rate search excerpts give platform rates, not a per-journey rate.

claims.claim: Administrators allocate Copilot Studio capacity to the Customer Insights - Journeys environment in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Before using AI agents, administrators need to make sure enough Copilot Studio capacity is allocated to the environment. Capacity allocation is managed in the Power Platform Admin Center.

claims.claim: AI Hub instructs administrators to configure message consumption limits to control Journey Creation Agent usage.
claims.quote: To control agent usage, configure *message consumption limits*. For more information, see [Manage capacity]

claims.claim: The allocation tutorial says disabling tenant-capacity draw caps an environment at its allocation.
claims.quote: when it's enabled, the environment continues to draw from unallocated tenant capacity after its own allocation is exhausted; when it's disabled, the environment is capped at its allocation.
claims.fix: Qualify the cap sentence with: 'The Manage capacity page also documents a separate Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan overage option; only when no overage source is enabled can the environment consume only its allocated prepaid credits.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-copilot-studio-messages-capacity#overage-management.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[2].note; Open questions
claims.claim: The allocation tutorial does not specifically name Journey Creation Agent when describing TenantPool enforcement.
claims.quote: Searched: Journey Creation Agent Copilot credits per journey price rate billing. Opened allocation tutorial, Journey Creation Agent, AI Hub prerequisites and Manage capacity; the feature links to capacity management, but the tutorial does not name this agent.

claims.claim: The cited prerequisite pages state no separate cost for allowing Anthropic or moving data across regions.
claims.quote: Searched: Anthropic AI provider subprocessor settings Microsoft 365 Power Platform API PowerShell enable external models; Journey Creation Agent Copilot credits per journey price rate billing. claims.quote: Searched: "Journey Creation Agent" "general availability" default. Read roadmap, Journey Creation Agent and AI Hub; sources give planned dates and preview enablement, not a general availability default.

claims.quote: Go to **Power Platform Admin Center** > **Copilot** > **Settings**. ... Scroll to the **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys** section. ... Select **AI agents**. ... Set **Use AI agents** to **On** for the selected environment or environment group.

claims.claim: An automation API for the Customer Insights - Journeys Use AI agents switch is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Use AI agents" "API" "Journeys"; Customer Insights Journeys AI Hub Use AI agents API msdynmkt_agentsettings Dataverse enable Journey Creation Agent. Opened AI Hub and Power Platform List tenant settings; no corresponding operation found.

claims.claim: The enablement path is Settings > AI Hub > Add and manage agents > Add an agent > Journey Creation Agent > Enable.
claims.quote: Select **Add an agent** and choose **Journey Creation Agent**. ... In the **Overview tab**, review how the agent works. ... To activate the agent, select **Enable**.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].ui.path with 'Settings > AI Hub > Add and manage agents > Add an agent > Journey Creation Agent > Overview tab > Enable', retaining https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/customer-insights/journeys/ai-hub.

claims.claim: No API for enabling Journey Creation Agent in AI Hub is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "msdynmkt_agentsettings" "Web API"; "msdynmkt_agentsettings" API enable; Customer Insights Journeys AI Hub Use AI agents API. Read AI Hub and returned Dataverse reference excerpts: msdyn_agentsetting is a different table, not proof for msdynmkt_agentsettings.

claims.claim: Credit allocation and tenant-pool draw are managed through Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Under **Products**, select **Copilot Studio**, and then select **Manage Copilot Credits**. ... Select the environment that you want to manage.
claims.fix: Append ' > environment' to controls[2].ui.path to include the documented selection of the environment whose allocation is being managed.

claims.claim: The printed PUT URL with entitlementId MCSMessages and a TenantPool enforcement rule is an executable allocation call.
claims.quote: scope = @{ environmentId = $environmentId } ... entitlementId = "MCSMessages" ... allocation = @{ quantity = 5000 } ... @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false }
claims.fix: The method, URL and 2024-10-01 version are documented, but replace the prose suffix with the actual required JSON body: 'PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01; Content-Type: application/json; Authorization: Bearer <token>; body: {"scope":{"environmentId":"<environment-id>"},"allocatedEntitlements":[{"entitlementId":"MCSMessages","allocation":{"quantity":<credits>},"enforcementRules":[{"ruleType":"TenantPool","enabled":false}]}]}'. Retain the current tutorial URL.

claims.claim: Anthropic is under Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > View all > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Available subprocessors for your organization.
claims.quote: select **Copilot** > **Settings** > **View all**. ... Select **AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors**. ... under **Available subprocessors for your organization**, select **Anthropic**, and **Save**.

claims.claim: No API for the Microsoft 365 Anthropic provider-access setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors" "Graph"; Anthropic AI provider subprocessor settings Microsoft 365 Power Platform API PowerShell enable external models. Opened connect-to-ai-subprocessor; no provider-setting Graph or PowerShell operation found.

claims.claim: The environment external-model settings are on Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features.
claims.quote: select **Manage**. ... select **Environments**, and then select the environment. ... select **Settings**. ... select **Product** > **Features**. ... turn each applicable model provider setting **On** or **Off**.

claims.claim: No API for allowing Anthropic models in a Power Platform environment is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Anthropic" "API" "tenant settings" Power Platform; Anthropic AI provider subprocessor settings Microsoft 365 Power Platform API PowerShell enable external models. Opened allow-llm-generative-responses and list-tenantsettings; no matching automation setting found.

claims.claim: Move data across regions is reached through Manage > Environments > environment > Generative AI features > Edit > Move data across regions.
claims.quote: select **Manage**. ... Select **Environments**. ... select the target environment. ... locate the **Generative AI features** card and select **Edit**. ... Select the **Move data across regions** checkbox.
claims.fix: Add to this row's note: 'The platform data-movement page says this checkbox is not displayed for environments in U.S. or government cloud regions.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/geographical-availability-copilot. The cited AI Hub prerequisites page gives the path without this qualification.

claims.claim: No API for the Move data across regions setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Move data across regions" "API" settings; "Move data across regions" "Power Platform API" "pac". Opened AI Hub prerequisites, geographical-availability-copilot and list-tenantsettings; found UI and environment-group guidance, not an API operation.

claims.claim: AI prompts is under Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > AI Builder > AI prompts.
claims.quote: select **Environments** > [*select an environment*] > **Settings** > **Product** > **Features**. ... under **AI Builder**, enable the **AI prompts** toggle.

claims.claim: No API for enabling the AI prompts environment setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "AI prompts" "PowerShell" "setting"; "AI prompts" "organization" "Web API"; "AI prompts" "Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironment". Opened ai-builder/administer and AI Hub prerequisites; found UI and group-rule configuration, not a matching API operation.

claims.claim: Tenants inside the EU Data Boundary cannot use Anthropic.
claims.quote: If your organization is in a region that has Anthropic as a subprocessor set to **Off** by default, you can choose to opt in so Claude models are available for your organization.
claims.fix: Replace the final question with: 'Will an Anthropic-free option or other model be offered for tenants whose policies prohibit processing outside the EU Data Boundary?' Being within the boundary does not itself prohibit opting in.

claims.claim: Nothing reaches users other than administrators and journey-building marketers.
claims.quote: Searched: "Journey Creation Agent" "other users". Read Journey Creation Agent and Responsible AI FAQ excerpts: they restrict visibility before publication, not all downstream effects after publication.
claims.fix: Remove '; nothing reaches other users' from the impact rationale. Retain the preceding description of the roles that configure and use the agent.

claims.where: Governance guidance: marketing roles and custom-role permissions
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to assign marketing roles and agent-settings permissions without a corresponding role-management control row.
claims.quote: Name the people who will hold the Marketing Manager or Marketing Professional role ... Give custom roles permission on the msdynmkt_agentsettings entity
claims.fix: Remove the two checklist bullets beginning 'Name the people who will hold' and 'Give custom roles permission'. The verified role requirements already remain in Risk assessment and the existing enablement-row note; do not add a control row.

claims.claim: The checklist tells readers to set a message consumption limit, but the table gives environment allocation rather than the separate agent-limit control.
claims.quote: enable Journey Creation Agent in **AI Hub** and set a message consumption limit. ... Copilot credits allocated to the environment and whether it can draw on tenant capacity
claims.fix: Remove 'and set a message consumption limit' from the At rollout checklist bullet. Keep the existing sourced discussion of consumption limits in Cost and licensing; do not add a control row.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Allocating credits and deciding on tenant-capacity draw establishes a cap before first use, although the page elsewhere says its applicability is unconfirmed.
claims.quote: 'so a cap exists before first use' conflicts with 'Learn does not say it governs this agent beyond the link from the Journey Creation Agent page, so confirm in a test environment'.
claims.fix: Replace the Before rollout bullet with: 'Allocate Copilot credits to the Customer Insights - Journeys environment and confirm the applicable consumption limits before first use.' This removes the promised cap without asserting an unverified enforcement outcome.
